topic_ko: 선행을 떠올리면 더 베풀지만, 겉모습을 의식하면 덜 베푼다
_note: 정답 분산: theme②, gist④, title③, claim⑤, implication①, blank②, order③, insert④, summary④. grammar/vocab/irrelevant는 위치 종속.

passage: The adult brain still holds on to a leaning toward good and fair conduct.
Merely thinking of oneself as a person who does good, and acting on that image, pushes one toward greater kindness later.
In a paid experiment with a hundred undergraduates, one group first listed their past good deeds.
When asked to give to a charity, that group handed over more than half of what they had earned in the study.
That was nearly double the amount given by students who had been told to remember their past wrongdoings.
Yet another pattern appeared among those who described not only their kindness but also the reactions it drew from others.
Those participants gave noticeably less than the ones who wrote only about the acts themselves.
Caring about how a good deed looks, in short, quietly drains the generosity out of it.
choices: why charities prefer college students as regular donors
how self-image and concern for appearances shape generosity
why writing about the past improves academic memory skills
how financial rewards change students' study habits over time
why people tend to forget the bad things they have done
theme.explanation_ko: 자신을 선한 사람으로 보는 자기 인식은 관대함을 키우고, 반대로 선행의 '겉모습'을 의식하면 관대함이 줄어든다는 글이다. ②가 주제.
theme.distractor_ko: ①기부자 모집, ③기억력 향상, ④학습 습관, ⑤망각 경향은 모두 본문의 초점이 아니다.

passage: Even grown-up brains keep a preference for continuing good and fair behavior.
Seeing ourselves as people who do good, and behaving that way, moves us toward greater good later on.
One paid study asked a hundred college students to write down either past good deeds or past bad deeds.
Those who listed good deeds later donated over half of their study earnings to charity.
That was almost twice what the students who had recalled bad deeds were willing to give.
A second contrast appeared inside the good-deed group itself.
Students who also described how others had reacted to their kindness gave far less than those who described only the acts.
Generosity, it seems, shrinks the moment a good deed becomes something to be seen.
choices: 선행은 보상이 클수록 더 자주 반복된다.
과거의 잘못을 반성해야 더 크게 베풀 수 있다.
기부 행동은 개인의 소득 수준에 의해 결정된다.
선행을 남에게 보이려 의식하면 오히려 관대함이 줄어든다.
학생들은 실험 상황에서 평소보다 더 많이 기부한다.
gist.explanation_ko: 선행 자체에 집중한 사람은 더 관대했고, 남들의 반응(겉모습)을 의식한 사람은 오히려 덜 기부했다. ④가 요지.
gist.distractor_ko: ①보상, ②반성, ③소득, ⑤실험 효과는 본문이 말한 대비와 다르다.

passage: A preference for good, fair behavior survives well into adulthood.
Simply picturing ourselves as people who do good deeds nudges us toward doing more of them.
A hundred paid college volunteers were split by what they were asked to remember.
Those who listed past kindnesses gave over half their earnings to a charity.
Those who listed past wrongs gave only about half as much.
But within the kind group, a subtle divide opened up.
Volunteers who dwelt on how others had reacted to their kindness donated far less than those who dwelt on the deed alone.
The purest giving, it turns out, is the giving that is not watching itself.
choices: Why Charities Should Pay Their Volunteers
Bad Memories: The Hidden Engine of Kindness
Give for the Deed, Not for the Applause
How College Students Learn to Save Money
The Limits of Memory in Moral Judgment
title.explanation_ko: 선행 자체(the deed)를 위해 베푼 사람이 더 관대했고, 남의 갈채(겉모습)를 의식한 사람은 덜 관대했다는 결론을 압축한 ③이 제목.
title.distractor_ko: ①자원봉사 보수, ②나쁜 기억 예찬, ④저축 습관, ⑤도덕 판단의 한계는 글의 결론과 어긋난다.

passage: We often assume that a good deed is a good deed, however it is framed.
Research on a hundred paid college students suggests otherwise.
Those who first listed their past kindnesses donated over half of their earnings to charity.
That was nearly twice the sum given by students who had recalled their past wrongs.
Inside the same experiment, however, a warning appeared.
Participants who described not just their kindness but the reactions it drew gave significantly less.
Attention paid to how a deed looks seems to compete with the impulse to give.
We should therefore practice kindness for its own sake rather than for the impression it makes.
choices: 기부액은 자신의 소득 범위 안에서 정해야 한다.
과거의 잘못을 자주 떠올리며 자신을 점검해야 한다.
자선 실험에 참여할 때는 보수를 받지 말아야 한다.
타인의 반응을 관찰하여 선행의 효과를 측정해야 한다.
선행은 남에게 보이기 위해서가 아니라 그 자체를 위해 해야 한다.
claim.explanation_ko: 마지막 문장이 곧 주장이다. 인상 관리가 아니라 선행 자체를 위해 베풀라는 ⑤가 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ①소득 기준, ②반성, ③무보수, ④효과 측정은 본문이 권하는 바가 아니다.

passage: The adult brain retains a preference for keeping good, fair behavior going.
Merely seeing ourselves as people who do good deeds motivates greater good later.
In a paid study of a hundred students, those who listed past good deeds gave over half their earnings to charity.
That was almost twice as much as those who had been asked to recall past bad deeds.
Yet students who also described how others responded to their kindness gave much less.
Their attention had drifted from the act toward the audience watching the act.
Generosity, it seems, weakens once a good deed starts to perform for a crowd.
The most giving people are those who never step onto that stage at all.
implication.underlined: never step onto that stage at all
choices: never treat their kindness as something to be watched
never speak about charity work in public settings
never accept payment for taking part in research
never remember the wrongs that others did to them
never compare their donations with other people's
implication.explanation_ko: '무대에 오르지 않는다'는 것은 선행을 남에게 보여 주는 공연으로 만들지 않는다는 뜻이다. 겉모습을 의식하지 않는다는 ①이 정답.
implication.distractor_ko: ②공개 발언, ③보수 거절, ④용서, ⑤비교는 '겉모습 의식'이라는 비유의 뜻과 다르다.

passage: Our adult brains retain a preference for perpetuating good, fair behavior.
Simply seeing ourselves as people who do good deeds motivates us to do greater good in the future.
In one paid study of a hundred college students, those who listed past good deeds donated over half of their study earnings.
That was almost twice as much as those who had been told to recall previous bad deeds.
But subjects who described not only their kindness but also how people responded gave significantly less.
They had begun to measure the deed by its effect on the audience rather than by the deed itself.
In other words, people concerned about appearances were less generous than those who cared about doing good for its own sake.
Real generosity, then, survives only when the giver stops asking how the gift will look.

blank.distractor_ko: ①기록, ③평판 좋은 단체, ④과거의 잘못, ⑤눈치 보기는 모두 오히려 겉모습을 더 의식하게 만드는 행동이다.

order.given: Our adult brains retain a preference for perpetuating good, fair behavior, and simply perceiving ourselves as people who do good deeds motivates us to do greater good in the future.

blocks.A: Within the very same study, though, a second and subtler split appeared among the participants who had written about their kindness.
blocks.B: Those who described not only how they had been nice but also how people had reacted donated far less than those who focused purely on the acts themselves.
blocks.C: Evidence comes from a paid study of a hundred college students, in which subjects who listed past good deeds gave over half their earnings to charity — almost twice what students recalling past bad deeds gave.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글의 일반 원리를 (C)가 'Evidence comes from ...'으로 실험을 들어 뒷받침하고, (A)가 'Within the very same study'로 그 실험 안의 두 번째 대비를 예고하며, (B)가 그 대비의 내용을 밝힌다. (C)-(A)-(B).
order.distractor_ko: (A)의 'the very same study'는 (C)에서 연구가 소개된 뒤라야 가리킬 대상이 생기고, (B)의 대비는 (A)가 예고한 뒤에 와야 자연스럽다.

passage: The adult brain preserves a preference for keeping good, fair behavior going.
Merely perceiving ourselves as people who do good deeds motivates greater good later.
In a paid study of a hundred college students, those who listed past good deeds gave over half their earnings to charity.
That was almost twice as much as students who had been asked to recall past bad deeds.
But participants who described how others had responded to their kindness gave significantly less.
They had begun to weigh the impact of the deed as much as the deed itself.
People concerned about appearances proved less generous than those who valued doing good for its own sake.
Motivation, in short, is strongest when the deed is its own reward.
summary.summary_template: The drive to do good was more __(A)__ among people who recalled their past virtues and attended only to their deeds, and weaker among people who were highly __(B)__ of how those deeds appeared to others.
summary.explanation_ko: 선행을 회상하고 행동 자체에 집중한 사람들에게서 동기가 더 (A)evident(뚜렷)했고, 선행의 겉모습을 (B)conscious(의식)한 사람들에게서는 약했다. ④가 정답.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)에 hidden·limited는 '두 배 기부'라는 결과와 반대이고, (B)에 careless·unaware는 겉모습을 '지나치게 의식했다'는 본문과 어긋난다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 성인이 된 우리의 뇌는 선하고 공정한 행동을 영속시키려는 선호를 유지한다.
writing.answer: Our adult brains retain a preference for perpetuating good, fair behavior.
writing.explanation_ko: 주어 Our adult brains + 동사 retain + 목적어 a preference + 전치사 for + 동명사 perpetuating 순서.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 겉모습에 신경 쓴 사람들이 덜 관대했다.
conditions: 비교급 less generous 를 사용할 것
writing.answer: People concerned about appearances were less generous.
writing.explanation_ko: 과거분사구 concerned about appearances가 People을 후치 수식하고, 보어로 비교급 less generous를 쓴다.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: Simply perceiving ourselves as people who do good deeds and behaving accordingly motivates us to do greater good in the future.
writing.answer: 단지 자신을 선행을 하는 사람으로 인식하고 그에 걸맞게 행동하는 것만으로도 우리는 미래에 더 큰 선을 행하도록 동기를 부여받는다.
writing.explanation_ko: 동명사구 두 개(perceiving ... / behaving ...)가 하나의 주어를 이루어 단수동사 motivates를 취한다. motivate + 목적어 + to부정사.

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 본문 내용을 바탕으로 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 한 단어씩 쓰시오. (본문의 표현을 그대로 옮기지 않아도 됨)
writing.summary: The motivation to do good was more (A)___________ in those who recalled their past virtues, and weaker in those who were highly (B)___________ of how their deeds appeared to others.
writing.explanation_ko: (A) 기부액이 거의 두 배였으므로 동기가 더 '뚜렷했다(evident)'. (B) 남들의 반응을 서술한 집단은 겉모습을 '의식했다(conscious)'.
